2027-03-23.title: Hasha Tuesday · Tuesday of Passion Week
readings: Moses, near death, commissions Joshua: “I will be with you”
The promise of entering his rest is still open
“And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself”
2027-03-23.alt: Hasha Week, the week of the Lord's Passion (Kashtanubhava Azhcha), which began on the evening of Hosanna Sunday. The Panchangam notes that the newly prepared Hasha Week lectionary gives an Old Testament reading, an Epistle and a Gospel for every hour of prayer this week; the readings below are the ones the Panchangam lists for the day.
2027-03-23.verse: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
theo: On Tuesday of Hasha Week the Church lets us hear the heart of Jesus as his hour comes near. Some Greeks have asked to see him, and he has spoken of the grain of wheat that must die to bear fruit. Then he says openly: “Now my soul is troubled.” He does not hide his fear from us. He is truly man, and he feels what we feel before suffering. But he does not run: “No, it is for this reason that I have come to this hour. Father, glorify your name.” A voice answers from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” St Augustine says that the Lord allowed his soul to be troubled so that the weak members of his body, when they are troubled, would not despair, but would find their own fear already carried by their Head (in substance). Then Jesus speaks of his Cross as a lifting up: “And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.” John adds: “He said this to indicate the kind of death he was to die.” The Cross is not only where he suffers; it is where he draws the whole world to himself.

The Old Testament reading takes us to the last days of Moses. “The Lord said to Moses, ‘Your time to die is near; call Joshua and present yourselves in the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him.’” Moses knows the people will be unfaithful after his death, so he writes a song to be a witness and lays the book of the law beside the ark. Then the Lord says to Joshua: “Be strong and bold, for you shall bring the Israelites into the land that I promised them; I will be with you.” Joshua's name in Hebrew is the same as the name of Jesus: “the Lord saves.” The Letter to the Hebrews draws the line from one to the other. Joshua led the people into the land, but not into God's final rest, for “if Joshua had given them rest, God would not speak later about another day.” That rest is still offered: “while the promise of entering his rest is still open, let us take care that none of you should seem to have failed to reach it... For we who have believed enter that rest.” Moses died outside the land. Jesus, the true Joshua, will die and rise, and lead us through death into the rest of God.

Jesus also says today: “The light is with you for a little longer. Walk while you have the light.” These are the days to walk in that light. Many families use Tuesday and Wednesday of Hasha Week to prepare for the great three days. The Church's own preparation is simple: finish your confession; make peace with anyone you have quarrelled with, since no one should come to the table of Pesaha with a grudge; and plan to be present for the services. On Thursday our Church celebrates Pesaha with the Holy Qurbono of the Lord's Supper and the washing of the feet. On Friday comes the long service of the Passion, with the readings of the hours, the procession and the veneration of the Cross. Saturday is the day of the Lord's rest in the tomb, and the night leads into Qyomtho, the Resurrection. At home, children can help prepare the house for Pesaha, and the family can read aloud tonight the words of Jesus about the grain of wheat (John 12:24).
outline: Ask: what do I do when I am afraid of what is coming?
Point 1 · Moses hands on the journey
“Be strong and bold... I will be with you.”
The fear of Jesus and his obedience.
Point 3 · Lifted up to draw all
The Cross that leads us into God's rest.

live: Before Thursday, speak or write to one person with whom you have a quarrel, and offer peace.
Walk while you have the light (John 12:35)
Tonight switch off the screens for one hour and spend part of it reading John 12 together.
2027-03-23.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, true Joshua, you lead your people through death into the rest of God. In your hour your soul was troubled, and yet you said: Father, glorify your name. When we are afraid, let us find our fear already carried by you. Lifted up on the Cross, draw us and all people to yourself. Keep us walking in your light in these holy days, and bring us to the joy of your Resurrection. Amen.
altar: On the altar the Lord who was lifted up draws us to himself; in the Holy Qurbono we already taste the rest that is still open to us.

quick: Before his death Moses commissioned Joshua: be strong and bold; I will be with you.
The promise of entering God's rest is still open to those who believe.
Jesus, troubled in soul, chose his hour; lifted up, he draws all people to himself.
2027-03-23.action: Offer peace today to someone you have quarrelled with.
2027-03-23.question: When I am troubled, do I run from my hour or give it to the Father?

family.explain: Jesus knew he was going to suffer. He said his heart was troubled. Jesus was not pretending; he really felt afraid, like we sometimes do. But he trusted his Father and did not run away. He said that when he was lifted up on the Cross he would draw everyone to himself, like a big hug for the whole world.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is afraid tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “When you are afraid, what can you say to God, as Jesus did?”

illus: A retired headmaster in Kottayam kept, for forty years, a small black notebook in which he wrote one sentence about every child who left his school. When he was dying, he called the young teacher who would take over the school archive and gave her the notebook. She asked what she should do with it. He said: read one page a day and pray for that child, wherever he or she is now. I cannot go with them any more. You will. She told the story at his funeral, holding the notebook, and said she was on page eleven.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in your hour your soul was troubled. We bring you our fears tonight. Amen.
share: Your time to die is near; call Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:14). What has someone handed on to me that I must carry forward?
While the promise of entering his rest is still open (Hebrews 4:1). Am I living as if God's rest is my goal?
Now my soul is troubled... Father, glorify your name (John 12:27–28). What fear can I give to the Father tonight?
interc: For all who are facing death or serious illness this week, that they may know the Lord is with them.
For those handing on responsibility in families, parishes and workplaces, and for those receiving it.
For all who are afraid of what is coming, that their fear may become trust.
For people of every nation, that the Lord lifted up on the Cross may draw them to himself.
For our Church in Hasha Week, that we may walk in the light while we have it.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up so that he might draw all people to himself. Give us courage in our hour, keep us faithful to the end, and lead us with him into your rest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel Jesus says: now my soul is troubled (John 12:27). Our Lord is truly man. He felt fear before his Passion. He does not ask us to pretend we are never afraid.

But he also says: no, it is for this reason that I have come to this hour. Father, glorify your name (John 12:27–28). Fear is not sin. Running from God's will is the danger. Jesus gives his fear to the Father.

Moses, near death, hands the people to Joshua, and God says: be strong and bold; I will be with you (Deuteronomy 31:23). Joshua bears the same name as Jesus. Hebrews tells us that the true rest of God is still open (Hebrews 4:1), and Jesus is the one who leads us into it.

And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself (John 12:32). This week let us look at the Cross and let him draw us: make peace before Pesaha, finish our confession, and walk in the light while we have it. Amen.
kids: Children, did you know that Jesus was afraid before he died? He said: my heart is troubled. But he talked to his Father, and he was brave. When you are scared, you can do what Jesus did: tell God, and ask him to help you be brave. Jesus said that on the Cross he would pull everyone close to him. He wants you close too!

intro: Theme: “And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”
On Hasha Tuesday: Moses hands on the journey, Jesus faces his hour, and the Cross draws all into God's rest.

sub: A song and a book as witness.
q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Thank God this week for someone who handed the faith on to you, and pray for whoever you must hand it on to.

sub: He does not run from his hour.
q: Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you disquieted within me? Hope in God; for I shall again praise him, my help and my God.
In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent submission.
points.apply: Tonight name one fear aloud before God and add: Father, glorify your name.

sub: The kind of death he was to die.
The rest that is still open.
q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God; for those who enter God’s rest also cease from their labors as God did from his.
points.apply: Spend five minutes each day until Friday simply looking at a crucifix.

concl: The Lord who feared still chose his hour, and his Cross draws the whole world.
Jesus, the true Joshua, leads us through death into the rest of God.
2027-03-23.resolve: Make peace and finish your confession before Pesaha, and look often at the Cross this week.
